messages:
jess thompson: quick thread — ran sim with the new policy-sanitizer adapter on the canary (~100k reqs). Observed ~0.7% rejects tagged as 'sanitizer:unhandled-header'. Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/abc123

liam chen: what's the sanitizer step today? is it applied pre-route or post-route in sidecar vs library modes?

jess thompson: canary config snippet we used:
```
sanitizer:
  strict: true
  drop_unknown: true
  whitelist:
    - x-tenant-id
    - x-client-version
```

nora gomez: that whitelist looks fine. My first thought: sim may be emitting legacy header variants (e.g. X-Request-ID vs x-request-id). The adapter currently treats headers case-sensitively.

pat (eng-runtime): yep — recent change in the router plugin ordering moved sanitizer to run before header-normalization in sidecar mode. In library mode normalization happened first. If sanitizer runs before normalization it sees unexpected header names.

maria (eng-ml): our sim harness always normalizes headers before passing them through adapters, so it never caught this ordering mismatch. I'll update the sim to run both orderings (normalize-first and sanitize-first) so we catch this class of regressions.

liam chen: we should avoid a hard fail in a canary for this class of incompatibility. Proposal: add `sanitizer.mode: permissive|strict`. Permissive emits warnings + a `sanitizer.warnings` header and increments a metric, strict returns 400.

jess thompson: agree. For an ongoing canary I'd prefer permissive + metric until we verify behavior across sidecar/library.

nora gomez: alternative short-term fix: expand whitelist semantics to include canonicalization variants, but that's brittle. Long-term fix is to canonicalize header names earlier in the pipeline and make sanitizer operate on a canonical map.

pat (eng-runtime): actionable plan I can take: 1) add `mode: permissive|strict` (default permissive for rollouts) and `sanitizer.rejects` + `sanitizer.warnings` metrics; 2) add a compatibility-mode flag for sidecar to optionally run normalization before sanitizer for 1-2 releases; 3) open PR to update adapter docs with explicit ordering guarantees. I'll try to keep the changes small and feature-flagged.

dev-bot: deploy canary 1744556600 -> cluster-us-west: started (10% traffic).

jess thompson: perfect — thanks Pat. Maria, once you update the sim harness, can you re-run the 100k-request sim against both ordering modes and post the reject/warning counts here? If permissive still shows high warnings (>1%), we should pause.

maria (eng-ml): will do. I expect to have sim results by EOD. I'll also add a small sim variant that injects header-name capitalization noise to stress this exact case.

liam chen: docs note: add a short paragraph under 'Adapter ordering' that lists expected ordering for hosted/dedicated/private deployments and how `mode` should be used during rollouts.

jess thompson: action items summary: Pat PR for permissive mode + metrics, Maria update sim and run both orders, Liam update docs, Nora follow-up on canonicalization RFC draft. Re-check in tomorrow architecture sync.

nora gomez: ok, I'll put the canonicalization RFC draft on the agenda and ping teams for feedback.

jess thompson: thanks all :thumbsup:
